cues.caption: Hello again, champ!
cues.text: Hello again, champ! Welcome back to Mentr Learn. Nice to see you.

cues.caption: Building on Chapter 1
cues.text: Yesterday we learned what a computer is. Today we go one step deeper.

cues.caption: Chapter 2 · How Computers Understand Us
cues.text: This is Chapter two. The lesson is: How Computers Understand Us.

cues.caption: Say with me: How Computers Understand Us
cues.text: Say it with me… How… Computers… Understand… Us.

cues.caption: Let's open the secret!
cues.text: Brilliant. Let's open the secret of computers.

cues.caption: Computers don't speak like us…
cues.text: Here is a puzzle. Computers are clever… but they do not speak Hindi or English like we do.

cues.caption: How do they understand us?
cues.text: So how do they understand games, photos, and messages?

cues.caption: ⏸ Your turn — make a guess!
cues.text: Pause. Guess for three seconds… how does a computer talk inside?

cues.caption: We'll prove it with switches
cues.text: Keep your guess. We will prove it with light switches.

cues.caption: Big idea: only TWO states
cues.text: The big idea is tiny and powerful. Inside a computer, everything is only two states.

cues.caption: Like a light switch: ON or OFF
cues.text: Like a light switch — ON… or OFF. That is all.

cues.caption: Say: On… or off!
cues.text: Say with me: On… or off. Only two choices!

cues.caption: ON = 1 · OFF = 0
cues.text: We write ON as the number one. We write OFF as the number zero.

cues.caption: 1 = on · 0 = off · Easy!
cues.text: One means on. Zero means off. Easy!

cues.caption: Three switches in a row
cues.text: Now imagine three light switches in a row. Left, middle, right.

cues.caption: Each switch = 1 or 0
cues.text: Each switch can be on or off. So each switch is a one or a zero.

cues.caption: off off on → 0 0 1
cues.text: Look: switch off, off, on — we write zero, zero, one.

cues.caption: on off on → 1 0 1
cues.text: Or on, off, on — we write one, zero, one.

cues.caption: Binary = language of TWO
cues.text: That pattern of ones and zeros is called binary. Bi means two. Two choices only.

cues.caption: Binary = light-switch language
cues.text: You do not need hard maths today. Just remember: binary is the computer's light-switch language.

cues.caption: Your turn — read the lights!
cues.text: Your turn to read! I show a pattern. You say the zeros and ones out loud.

cues.caption: Pattern 1: 0 0 1
cues.text: Pattern one: off, off, on. You say… zero, zero, one!

cues.caption: Pattern 2: 1 1 0
cues.text: Pattern two: on, on, off. You say… one, one, zero!

cues.caption: Pattern 3: 1 0 1
cues.text: Pattern three: on, off, on. You say… one, zero, one!

cues.caption: Super! Tiny bits of information
cues.text: Super reading. That is how computers store tiny bits of information.

cues.caption: Practice check
cues.text: Practice check — same kind of question you will see later.

cues.caption: What does 1 0 1 mean?
cues.text: If one means on, what does one-zero-one mean on three lights?

cues.caption: Think: left · middle · right
cues.text: Think… left on, middle off, right on.

cues.caption: Answer: ON · OFF · ON ✓
cues.text: Yes! One-zero-one means on, off, on. Three lights telling a tiny story.

cues.caption: Photos, games, messages → 0s & 1s
cues.text: Why learn this? Because every photo, every game, every message becomes ones and zeros inside.

cues.caption: Words ↔ on/off ↔ pictures & sound
cues.text: Your brain uses words. The computer uses on and off — then turns it back into pictures and sound for you.

cues.caption: Binary = light-switch language!
cues.text: So when someone says binary, you can smile and say: light-switch language!

cues.caption: ON = 1 · OFF = 0
cues.text: Lock it in. Computers understand on and off. On is one. Off is zero.

cues.caption: Binary = the computer's language
cues.text: A row of ones and zeros is binary — the computer's special language.

cues.caption: 101 → on, off, on
cues.text: You can read a short pattern like one-zero-one as on, off, on.

cues.caption: Chapter 2 complete!
cues.text: Chapter two done. How Computers Understand Us — excellent work today!
